n.quote:
A linear regression (stats 4.0.2 in R)7 has been conducted to assess the relation between
L1 Spanish speakers’ and learners’ frequency of past tokens. As may be observed in
Figure 5, results show an R2 value of 0.78 (r = 0.88, p < 2.2e-16) for the relation
between L1 and L2 frequency regarding the 300 verbs in the preterit. The relation for
the 129 verbs in the imperfect shows an R2 value of 0.70 (r = 0.83, p < 2.2e-16), ... The contingent frequency analysis considers the association between verbs and the
preterit or imperfect. We have conducted a DCA (Gries and Stefanowitsch 2004) which
yields results for the association between lemmas and the constructions with which they
occur, such as the preterit and the imperfect.

notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical full article text: title Preterit-imperfect acquisition in L2 Spanish writing: Moving beyond lexical aspect; all six named authors match; DOI 10.32714/ricl.10.01.08 and Research in Corpus Linguistics 10/1: 156–184 (2022) appear on the first page. Document includes methods, results, discussion, and references, rather than an abstract-only parse. No PDF was supplied. Only n_r is assigned; all other fields are unassigned placeholders. The page-20 locator supplies a candidate analytic count of 300 preterit verbs for token-frequency regression, not participant N. The neutral description instead specifies distinctiveness/contingent frequency, analyzed separately by DCA and verb-specific binomial tests. No unique overall target test follows from both clues, so the regression count is retained only as a candidate for parent field-scope review. Candidate verb counts are printed directly; no sum or df inference performed. No regression statistic has been assigned to the distinctiveness target. The 820 L1 and 611 L2 essays/participants on p. 167 and eight longitudinal participants on pp. 168–169 are separate contributor roles, not interchangeable with the verb-level analytic counts.
